108	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining_for_product'
109	                  },
110	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel, productName: currentLowestStockLevelProductName}
111	              )
112	            : intl.formatMessage(
113	                  {
114	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left!',
115	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining'
116	                  },
117	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel}
118	              )
119	    }
120	
121	    // showInventoryMessage controls if add to cart button is disabled
122	    const showInventoryMessage =
123	        (variant || isProductABundle || isStandardProduct) &&
124	        (currentIsOutOfStock || currentUnfulfillable)
125	    const inventoryMessage =
126	        (currentIsOutOfStock && inventoryMessages[OUT_OF_STOCK]) ||
127	        (currentUnfulfillable && inventoryMessages[UNFULFILLABLE])

129	    // If the `initialQuantity` changes, update the state. This typically happens
130	    // when either the master product changes, or the inventory of the product changes
131	    // from out-of-stock to in-stock or vice versa.

152	                        href: isControlled

renders. That was the one surface worth worrying about (a shopper sees it after paying).

**Two requirements for the override, both load-bearing:**
1. **Keep the defaults-then-spread order.** Callers set their own geometry —
   `order-summary` does `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` — and must keep winning.
   Write `<Box width={zimmDefault} {...props}>`, never the reverse, or you break layouts that work
   today. `item-image`, `item-attributes` and `item-price` already have it right.
2. **Fix `item-name` while in there.** Base is `<Link {...props} color="black.600">` — spread
   *before* the colour, so no caller can ever override it. Move the spread after; no base caller
   passes `color`, so nothing changes for them.

**Deferred consequence, accepted:** when checkout is designed it will inherit cart-derived
line-item styling it never specified. Whoever picks up checkout should know why it already looks
part-branded.

## Scale line

This was a targeted REWORK verification (the 7 claimed fixes + the "Also confirm" build-health/file-scope list), not a from-scratch full-diff sweep — matching exactly what the task specified. All 7 claims and all "Also confirm" items were run; nothing from the given scope was dropped. Method note: my first sub-agent dispatch (`fork`, for Claim 1) errored on every subsequent nested dispatch — "Fork is not available inside a forked worker" — so I did Claim 1 myself directly (source-trace + a real empirical falsification, see below) and used four non-fork `general-purpose` agents for the other buckets instead. To compensate for losing the fork's shared-context/higher-trust properties, I independently re-verified the two highest-stakes items myself from scratch (Claim 6's Chakra source, Claim 7's grep, the file-scope discrepancy, and both critical test files' exact assertions) rather than taking any single agent's word — full detail below. Net effect: coverage matches the brief; nothing was skipped because of the tooling hiccup.

---

## Claim 1 — Story crash fix (two stacked bugs) — **CONFIRMED**, most rigorously verified item

Did this one myself, not delegated. `index.stories.tsx`: `variants: []` present on both `MOCK_LINE_ITEM` (line 118) and `MOCK_LINE_ITEM_TWO` (line 138); `StoreLocatorProvider` (from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts`) wraps the tree nested inside `MultiSiteProvider` (lines 74-83: `MemoryRouter > MultiSiteProvider > StoreLocatorProvider > CommerceProviders > Story`).

`index.stories.test.tsx` — traced the real hook chain against actual `node_modules` source, not the docblock's own say-so:
- `use-derived-product.js:13,66` imports `useSelectedStore` from its own direct sub-path (not the barrel) and calls it unconditionally: `const {selectedStore} = useSelectedStore()`.
- `use-selected-store.js:10,19-21` imports `StoreLocatorContext` from `.../app/contexts/store-locator-provider` directly (never the barrel) and throws `'useSelectedStore must be used within a StoreLocatorProvider'` if context is falsy — exact match to the claimed error.
- `use-variation-attributes.js:74-82`'s `isVariantValueOrderable` does `product.variants.filter(...)` with **zero guard** — confirmed directly in source.
- The test's `vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks', ...)` factory uses `vi.importActual` to fetch the **real** `useDerivedProduct`, only stubbing `useCurrency`. Since `use-derived-product.js` imports `useVariationAttributes`/`useSelectedStore` via direct sub-paths (not the mocked barrel), both run for real, transitively. `useVariationAttributes`/`isVariantValueOrderable` are never separately mocked anywhere in the file. This is exactly the claim: only `use-multi-site`/`useCurrency`/genuinely-unrelated SDK plumbing (`useStores`, `promo-popover`) are mocked — the two bugs' own code paths are never touched by a mock.
- `app/contexts/index.js:47-50` really is a `.js` file with inline JSX (`<MultiSiteContext.Provider>...</MultiSiteContext.Provider>`) — confirmed directly, including that line 49 is a JSX closing tag, matching the claimed failure line.

**Empirical falsification** (not just source-reading): backed up the untracked test file (md5 `4c4aed4b...`), commented out `variants: []` in its `MOCK_LINE_ITEM`, reran — both tests failed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')`, the exact predicted mechanism. Restored the file from backup; `diff` against the backup showed zero differences, md5 matched, tests passed again (2/2). Real pasted output both ways.

No finding. This is a genuinely real, well-verified fix.

## Claim 2 — item-variant/index.test.tsx CartItemVariantAttributes coverage — **CONFIRMED**

Independently read `index.test.tsx:185-196` myself (byte-identical to what the dispatched agent quoted): asserts `getByText('Colour: Lilac Sand')` and `getByText('Size: One Size')` present, **and** `queryByText('Lilac Sand, One Size')` absent — a real per-key-vs-combined differentiation, not a smoke render. Real test run: 9/9 passed.

## Claim 3 — item-variant.css.ts fontWeight removal — **CONFIRMED**

Read the `colourSize` part myself directly (item-variant.css.ts:73-87) — no `fontWeight` key. Dispatched agent traced `typography.ts`'s `caption` textStyle to `fontWeight: fontWeights.medium` = `'500'` (typography.ts:31-34,142-149), confirming the override really was redundant. One trivial imprecision (not a defect): the implementer's comment says both session-notes.md citations are headed "RESOLVED" — only §11.10's heading literally says that; §11.2 doesn't. Cosmetic only.

## Claim 4 — hideStepperAndActions prop — **CONFIRMED**, dual-verified

Read `product-item/index.tsx:100-232` myself in full. Confirmed byte-for-byte against the dispatched agent's quotes: optional boolean (line 123), defaults falsy (line 146), and **both** `deliveryActions` render sites gated identically (lines 174-176 desktop, 179-181 mobile) — the specific risk the brief called out. Stepper (185-197), `secondaryActions` (217), and **both** `primaryAction` sites (203, 221-225) also gated. Read `index.test.tsx:161-203` myself — matches quoted code exactly: a real DOM-absence test (`.not.toBeInTheDocument()` on stepper text + all three action slots) and a real presence test for the omitted-prop path. `GiftCard` story confirmed in `index.stories.tsx:173-180`. Real test run: 3/3 passed.

## Claim 5 — item-price.tsx test coverage — **CONFIRMED**

Coverage combined in `index.test.tsx` (confirmed no separate item-price test file exists). Three tests with real differentiating assertions: isDesktop DOM-order reversal via `compareDocumentPosition`, `isOnSale` gap `0px` vs `var(--chakra-space-1)`, and the price recipe's textStyle (`fontSize: '0.875rem', fontWeight: '500'`) — none are bare smoke renders.

## Claim 6 — product-item.css.ts docblock, Chakra Flex/Text precedence — **CONFIRMED**, dual-verified against real source

Read the actual compiled Chakra source myself independently: `@chakra-ui/layout/dist/chunk-MPFPK3CX.mjs` (Flex) — `jsx(chakra.div, { ref, __css: styles, ...rest })`, `__css` **before** `...rest`. `chunk-P74GIWPW.mjs` (Text) — `jsx(chakra.p, { ref, ..., ...rest, __css: styles })`, `__css` **after** `...rest`. This exactly confirms the docblock: same object-literal-key-collision mechanism, winner reversed — Flex lets a caller's `__css` (via `rest`) erase Flex's own styles; Text's own `__css` erases the caller's. Also checked `@chakra-ui/system/dist/chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`'s `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — `sx` last, always wins, matching the docblock's claim that `sx` sidesteps the whole hazard. The dispatched agent reached the identical conclusion independently, byte-for-byte matching source quotes.

## Claim 7 — ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE constant — **CONFIRMED**, dual-verified

Ran my own `grep -rn "'ZimmCartItemVariant'" overrides/` — exactly one hit, at `item-variant.css.ts:17` where it's defined. Confirmed `item-image.tsx`, `item-attributes.tsx`, `item-price.tsx` each import `ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE` from `./item-variant.css` and use it at their `useMultiStyleConfig` call — no retyped literal anywhere. Matches the dispatched agent's independent grep exactly. (Aside, not a finding: `product-item/index.tsx` has its own **local** `const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem'` — correct, since that recipe has exactly one consumer, so there's nothing to deduplicate.)

## Build health — **CONFIRMED, all numbers match claims exactly**

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: empty output, exit 0. Clean.
- `npm run test`: **86 files / 1247 tests, all passing** — matches the claimed 85→86 / 1238→1247 delta exactly (pre-rework baseline itself wasn't re-verified — see gaps below — but the current-state numbers are a real, confirmed match).
- `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`: exactly 7 unacknowledged violations. The two claimed pre-existing-in-touched-files ones (item-image.tsx `fontSize="10px"` ×2, item-price.tsx `PricePerItem` fontSize) were confirmed via `git diff -U0` to be unchanged context lines, not part of this round's added lines.
- `recipeGuards.test.ts`: 6/6 passed. `recipeParts.test.ts`: 41/41 passed — I independently read its own docblock (line 28: "Scope: `overrides/app/components/**` — every co-located `<name>.css.ts`") and confirmed both new recipes fall inside it.

## File scope — **one real, but benign, finding: 🟡 should-fix (process/disclosure), not a code defect**

All 10 expected files confirmed present. But — flagged from the git-status snapshot at session start and chased down independently by me (not just the dispatched agent): **two additional files are modified and were never named in the task's file list or the 7 claims**:

- `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — read the full diff myself: purely additive, two new imports + two new map entries (`ZimmCartItem`, `ZimmCartItemVariant`). Required by this repo's own co-location-registration rule. Not a finding.
- `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-name.tsx` — read the full diff myself: fixes a prop-spread-order bug (`color` now precedes `{...props}`, matching its siblings) and restyles `fontSize="md"` → `textStyle="productNames"`. **This is not scope creep** — I grepped `.claude/session-notes.md` myself and found it explicitly pre-planned at line 362: *"Fix `item-name` while in there. Base is `<Link {...props} color=\"black.600\">` — spread before the colour... Move the spread after."* It also has real, passing test coverage (`item-variant/index.test.tsx`'s `CartItemVariantName — spread-order bug fix` tests, which I read directly and confirmed exist and pass).

**Verdict on this finding:** 🟡 should-fix, **UNIFORM** risk (not this instance's content, which is correct) — the Implementer's "7 claimed fixes" summary under-disclosed the full diff by two files. This time both turned out legitimate on inspection, but the pattern of an incomplete self-reported change list is exactly the kind of gap that lets something less benign slip through a future round unnoticed, across the remaining 13 commits of this 18-commit plan. Worth naming explicitly to the Implementer, not just quietly absorbing.

`data-testid` on `product-item/index.tsx` confirmed untouched (context line only, no +/-). No `.stories.tsx` files added for item-image/item-name/item-attributes/item-price (confirmed via `find`, zero results).

Recipe namespacing (`ZimmCartItem`/`ZimmCartItemVariant`, both Zimm-prefixed), import correctness, no bare Chakra token keys in new lines, no responsive-array shorthand — all confirmed clean, independently, by both the dispatched agent and my own direct read of all three item-variant sibling diffs plus `product-item/index.tsx`'s full import block (lines 71-94, matching its own documented import-path-rewrite reasoning exactly).

---

- Directly attacked Claim 1 (the "most important" one) with a real break-it-and-watch-it-fail experiment, not just reasoning — it failed exactly as predicted, then was cleanly reverted (md5-verified).
